newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BEKAERT COULD FALL ANOTHER 15% - ANALYSTS.
newsitem.headline: BEKAERT COULD FALL ANOTHER 15% - ANALYSTS.

text.p: Shares in Belgian steel cord and wire maker Bekaert deepened their losses on Wednesday, falling almost six percent as investors reacted nervously to a company warning on profits and increased competition.
The share was down 5.4 percent at 18,750 francs at 1315 GMT after closing down 13.4 percent yesterday.
"I'm not surprised if the share falls to 16,000 francs...at the moment the share still remains expensive," said analyst Isabelle Defranne at broker Mignon, Hannart and Declerck.
Analyst Jean-Marie Caucheteux at Banque Bruxelles Lambert said the share could fall to 16,500 francs in the coming days.

Bekaert said on Monday it had revised down its estimated 1996 net current profits after being hit by compertition from cheap eastern European steel cord. This caused analysts to revise down their earnings per share (EPS) forecasts.
"There is a serious threat for Bekaert from cheap steel quality from eastern Europe," said Caucheteux, who said the share was now a 'sell'.
Broker Vermeulen Raemdonck revised down its EPS for 1996 from 1,035 francs to 712 and for 1997 to 1,100 francs. "We reiterate our 'sell' recommendation on Bekaert," it said.
Broker Mignon, Hannart and Declerck revised its 1996 EPS net current profit forecast down to 795 francs, but retained its 1997 EPS forecast at 1,135 francs.
Bekaert said the restructuring plan would cost 1.6 to 1.8 billion francs.
This would wipe out 1996 net current profit of 1.6 billion as forecast by analysts.
Analysts expect bottom-line results to be lifted to 2.3 billion francs by a capital gain on the sale of shares in Japanese tyre-maker Bridgestone Metalpha Corp .
The restructuring involves cutting production staff and writing-off some machinery and installations which have not completely been depreciated.
"It's difficult to say if the restructuring will exert a significant impact in 1997 as past restructuring programmes have shown mixed results," said Defranne.
